answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases as a result has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the juniper collateral is checked against the quartz claim at intake, the mirror audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 8 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
